mainTopic: Conduct during marital intimacy and how it affects children, the ruling against יוחנן בן דהבאי, and the opening of the new פרק on four kinds of non-binding vows.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a story. People asked אימא שלום, wife of רבי אליעזר, why her children were so beautiful. She described her husband's modest conduct, which included speaking with her during intimacy. This challenged יוחנן בן דהבאי's warning against speaking. The גמרא answers that only talk about other matters is a problem. רבי יוחנן then rules that the הלכה does not follow יוחנן בן דהבאי at all, comparing a couple's private life to meat or fish a person may prepare as he likes. אמימר explains that the 'ministering angels' behind those rules were really חכמים, and stories about רבי and רב show the same ruling in real cases. רבי teaches that a man must not think of another woman during intimacy, even his own second wife. רבי לוי lists the flawed situations that produce rebellious children, and the גמרא explains that a wife who gently hints is praised, unlike the brazen חצופה. The פרק ואלו מותרין then closes, and a new משנה begins listing four kinds of vows that חכמים treat as not binding, starting with a haggling example.

steps.title: אימא שלום describes her husband's modest conduct
steps.stepSummary: The story continues: asked why her children are so beautiful, אימא שלום explains that רבי אליעזר was intimate with her only at midnight, very modestly, and spoke with her at that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: (People asked her:) Why are your children so very beautiful? She answered them: My husband is not intimate with me at the beginning of the night or at the end of the night, only at midnight. And when he is intimate, he uncovers a handbreadth and covers a handbreadth, and he acts like someone being forced by a demon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the story it brought to challenge יוחנן בן דהבאי. אימא שלום explains the special conduct of her husband, רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מספר literally means 'talks,' and here it refers to being intimate while talking. That is the point of the challenge: a great sage like רבי אליעזר spoke during relations, and his children came out beautiful, the opposite of what יוחנן בן דהבאי warned.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'talks'; here a modest way of saying being intimate while talking
Forced by a demon; acting in a hurried, fearful way

steps.confusionAlert: This section opens in the middle of a sentence. The question 'are your children so beautiful?' was asked of אימא שלום, wife of רבי אליעזר. The story is being used as a challenge, not just told as a nice story.

phrases.english: Are your children so very beautiful?
phrases.notes: People are asking this of אימא שלום, wife of רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: She said to them:
He does not converse with me
phrases.notes: 'Converse' is a gentle way of saying he is intimate with her, and he talks with her while doing so.

phrases.english: not at the beginning of the night,
and not at the end of the night,
but rather at midnight.
And when he converses,
he uncovers a handbreadth and covers a handbreadth,
and he seems like one who is being forced by a demon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge against יוחנן בן דהבאי that began just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: יוחנן בן דהבאי's rule that speaking during relations harms the children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר, a great sage, spoke with his wife during relations, and their children were especially beautiful. So speaking cannot be forbidden or harmful.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר explains the reason for his conduct
steps.stepSummary: אימא שלום reports that when she asked her husband why he acted this way, he said it was so he would not think of another woman, which would harm the children.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I asked him: What is the reason? And he told me: So that I will not set my eyes on another woman, which would bring his children close to a kind of ממזרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי אליעזר's reason for his modesty. This completes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His goal was to keep his thoughts only on his wife. Thinking of another woman at that time would make the children spiritually similar to ממזרים. This shows his conduct was deliberate and holy, which makes the challenge stronger: if he still spoke with her, speaking must be acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Set my eyes on; think about
The status or nature of a ממזר

phrases.english: And I said to him: What is the reason?
And he said to me:
So that I will not set my eyes
on another woman,
and his children would end up coming close to ממזר status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story from step 1 by giving רבי אליעזר's reason, which makes the challenge complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: יוחנן בן דהבאי's rule against speaking during relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sage this careful about holiness still spoke with his wife, so speaking cannot be harmful.

steps.title: Speech about intimacy is different from other talk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר's speech was about the relationship itself, which is allowed, while יוחנן בן דהבאי was warning about talking of other matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This (what רבי אליעזר did) was speech about matters of intimacy. That (what יוחנן בן דהבאי warned against) is speech about other matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the two sources are talking about different kinds of speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction disappears once we see that 'speaking' is not one thing. Talking about the relationship itself, which brings husband and wife closer, is fine. Talking about unrelated matters at that time is what יוחנן בן דהבאי warned against.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the standard opening of an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is regarding matters of intimacy,
phrases.notes: 'This' means רבי אליעזר's speech in the story.

phrases.english: that is regarding other matters.
phrases.notes: 'That' means the speech יוחנן בן דהבאי warned against.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 1-2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources refer to different kinds of speech.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed יוחנן בן דהבאי forbade all speech during relations, so רבי אליעזר's speaking seemed to contradict him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only speech about unrelated matters is a problem. Speech about the relationship itself is allowed, as רבי אליעזר did.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow יוחנן בן דהבאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the חכמים rejected יוחנן בן דהבאי's rules: a husband may conduct his private life with his wife as he wishes, like meat or fish a person may prepare however he likes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: These are the words of יוחנן בן דהבאי, but the חכמים said: The הלכה is not like יוחנן בן דהבאי. Rather, whatever a man wants to do with his wife, he may do. It is like meat that comes from the butcher: if he wants to eat it salted, he eats it; roasted, he eats it; cooked, he eats it; boiled, he eats it. And the same is true of fish that comes from the fisherman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the final ruling: the חכמים do not accept יוחנן בן דהבאי's restrictions. He backs this up with a parable about food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the גמרא worked to explain יוחנן בן דהבאי, רבי יוחנן says the הלכה doesn't follow him at all. These matters are left to the couple, just as a person who brings home meat or fish may prepare it in any way he likes.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not (like this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from אימא שלום was answered by splitting kinds of speech. But in the end, רבי יוחנן reports that the חכמים do not follow יוחנן בן דהבאי's restrictions at all. A husband and wife may conduct their private life as they wish, like the meat and fish parable.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the answer in step 3 is the final word. It only showed that יוחנן בן דהבאי could be explained. רבי יוחנן then says the הלכה does not follow him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical halachic outcome: the restrictions of יוחנן בן דהבאי are not binding according to the חכמים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is the statement of Yochanan ben Dehavai,
but the Sages said:
The halacha is not like Yochanan ben Dehavai,
rather, whatever a man wishes
to do with his wife, he may do.
A parable: like meat that comes from the butcher shop,
if he wants to eat it with salt, he eats it.
Roasted, he eats it.
Cooked, he eats it.
Boiled, he eats it.
And likewise fish that comes from the fisherman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי, אֲבָל אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge was answered, רבי יוחנן gives the final ruling that sets aside יוחנן בן דהבאי's opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה does not follow יוחנן בן דהבאי; a man may conduct his marital life with his wife as he wishes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Like meat from the butcher or fish from the fisherman, which may be prepared in any way, a couple's private conduct is not bound by יוחנן בן דהבאי's restrictions.

steps.title: The 'ministering angels' were really the Sages
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says the 'ministering angels' who taught יוחנן בן דהבאי his rules were actually human חכמים. He proves it: if real angels had said it, רבי יוחנן could not have rejected those rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: Who are these 'ministering angels'? The חכמים. Because if you say they were real angels, why would רבי יוחנן say the הלכה is not like יוחנן בן דהבאי? Angels surely know more about how a baby is formed!
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר explains who the 'ministering angels' were. They were human חכמים, not real angels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ruled against יוחנן בן דהבאי (step 4). If real angels had given those rules, nobody could overrule them, since angels know far more about how a baby is formed. So the 'angels' must have been human sages, and other sages are allowed to disagree with them.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is arguing with angels. אמימר's whole point is that these were people with an honorary title, so other חכמים could disagree with them.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
Who are the "ministering angels"? The Sages.
For if you say actual ministering angels,
why did Rabbi Yochanan say
the halacha is not like Yochanan ben Dehavai?
But they are experts
in the forming of the baby, more [than we are]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יוחנן could reject rules said to come from angels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'ministering angels' were human חכמים, which is why their view can be overruled.

steps.title: Why the Sages are called angels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים would be called 'ministering angels.' It answers that they stand out the way angels do.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why are they called ministering angels? Because they stand out like ministering angels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why human sages get the name 'ministering angels.' It answers right away: they are recognizable and stand apart, like angels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we say the 'angels' are people, we need to explain the title. The answer is that the חכמים are marked out and distinguished, so the name is a title of honor.

keyTerms.meaning: because they are distinguished, they stand out

phrases.english: And why do they call them ministering angels?
Because they stand out like ministering angels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on אמימר's explanation by justifying the title.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why human sages would be called 'ministering angels.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because they stand out and are distinguished like angels.

steps.title: A woman complains to רבי and he cannot help
steps.stepSummary: A woman complains to רבי that her husband was intimate with her in an unusual way. רבי tells her the תורה permits it, so he cannot do anything for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before רבי and said: My teacher, I set a table for him and he turned it over! He said to her: My daughter, the תורה permitted you to him. What can I do for you?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the same ruling as step 4 in a real case. רבי tells a woman that her husband's unusual conduct is permitted by the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman uses polite code language for intimacy done in an unusual manner. רבי answers that the תורה permitted husband and wife to each other, so a rabbi has no power to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: I set a table for him (a polite way of referring to intimacy)

phrases.english: A certain woman who came before Rabbi
said to him: My teacher,
I set a table for him and he turned it over!
phrases.notes: This is polite code language. She means he was intimate with her in an unusual way.

phrases.english: He said to her: My daughter,
the Torah permitted you [to him],
and what can I do for you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies the conclusion of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What the תורה permits between husband and wife, a rabbi cannot forbid.

steps.title: The same complaint before רב: like a fish
steps.stepSummary: A similar woman complains to רב. He answers that this is no different from a fish, which a person may prepare however he likes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before רב and said: My teacher, I set a table for him and he turned it over! He said: How is this different from a fish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, matching story. רב uses the fish comparison from step 4 to answer the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's answer brings back the picture from step 4: just as a person may eat a fish however he wishes, a husband may conduct private life with his wife as he wishes. The two stories together show that both רבי and רב ruled this way in real cases.

phrases.english: A certain woman who came before Rav
said to him: My teacher,
I set a table for him and he turned it over!
He said: How is this different from a fish?
phrases.notes: This echoes רבי יוחנן's comparison to fish that a person may prepare any way he likes.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule, together with both stories, shows that a husband and wife's private life is not limited by יוחנן בן דהבאי's restrictions.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 7, using the fish comparison from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Private conduct between husband and wife is like a fish, prepared however one wishes.

steps.title: Do not think of another woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from the פסוק 'do not go after your heart' that a man must not be with one woman while thinking of another.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall not go after your heart.' From here רבי said: A person should not drink from this cup while setting his eyes on another cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching based on a פסוק. A man must not be intimate with one woman while thinking about another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a limit next to the freedom given in steps 7 and 8. The 'cup' is picture language for a woman. The rule matches רבי אליעזר's concern in step 2, that thinking of another woman during intimacy is harmful.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall not go after (stray after)

phrases.english: "And you shall not go after your own heart"
From here Rabbi said:
A person should not drink from this cup
while setting his eyes on another cup.
phrases.notes: This is picture language: being with one woman while thinking about a different one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ אַחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם, מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit after the freedom described in steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not be intimate with one woman while thinking of another.

steps.title: Even with his own two wives
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says רבי's rule is needed for a surprising case: even if both women are his wives, he may not think of one while with the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This was not needed for an ordinary case. It is needed to teach that it applies even to his own two wives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains what רבי's teaching adds. It forbids thinking of the other woman even when she is also his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thinking of a woman who is forbidden to him is obviously wrong, so רבי did not need to teach that. רבינא says the new point is that even when both women are permitted to him, he must not think of one while with the other.
steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying the rule applies only to two wives. He means the rule is so strong that it applies even to them, and all the more to any other woman.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
It is not needed [for an ordinary case],
rather, [it teaches] that even with his two wives [this applies].

steps.whatToRemember: A man must not think of another woman during intimacy, even if that other woman is also his wife.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא, אֶלָּא דַּאֲפִילּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the new point added by רבי's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule applies even when both women are his wives.

steps.title: Rebels come from nine flawed traits
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק about purging the rebels, רבי לוי says these are children born from nine flawed traits, which he gives as a memory code. The list is explained next.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And I will purge from among you the rebels and those who sin against Me.' רבי לוי said: These are children of nine traits, children of אסנ"ת משגע"ח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי opens a new list: nine kinds of improper intimacy that produce rebellious children. He only gives a memory code here, which sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of rebels who will be removed from the people. רבי לוי connects them to the way they were conceived, with each letter of the code standing for one flawed trait. This continues the theme that the parents' conduct during intimacy affects the children.

phrases.english: "And I will purge from among you the rebels and those who sin against Me"
Rabbi Levi said:
These are children of nine traits,
children of Aleph-Samekh-Nun-Tav Mem-Shin-Gimmel-Ayin-Chet.
phrases.notes: This is a memory code. Each letter stands for one of the nine traits, and the גמרא spells them out next.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָרוֹתִי מִכֶּם הַמֹּרְדִים וְהַפּוֹשְׁעִים בִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of conduct during intimacy and opens a new list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rebellious children come from nine improper kinds of intimacy, given by the code אסנ"ת משגע"ח.

steps.title: The list of flawed traits spelled out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists the flawed situations whose children are called 'rebels': fear, force, hatred, נידוי, substitution, quarreling, drunkenness, a wife already divorced in his heart, confusion, and a brazen wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the children of: fear, a forced woman, a hated woman, נידוי, substitution, quarreling, drunkenness, a wife divorced in the heart, mix-up, and a brazen woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the list that רבי לוי's memory code stood for in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item describes a bad state of mind or a bad relationship at the time of intimacy. Examples are fear, hatred, drunkenness, or thinking of another woman. Step 9 already taught the 'substitution' item, being with one woman while thinking of another. The last item, 'חצופה', will be challenged next.

keyTerms.meaning: Fear. The wife was afraid of her husband.
Substitution. He thought of a different woman.
A wife he had already decided in his heart to divorce.
A mix-up. He did not know which woman he was with.
A brazen woman who openly demands intimacy.

steps.confusionAlert: Count carefully: ten items appear here, even though רבי לוי spoke of nine traits. The גמרא does not deal with this here, so don't let it throw you off.

phrases.english: Children of fear, children of a woman who was forced,
children of a hated woman, children of נידוי (ban),
children of substitution, children of quarreling,
phrases.notes: Substitution is the case from step 9: he was with one woman while thinking of another.

phrases.english: children of drunkenness, children of a woman divorced in the heart,
children of a mix-up, children of a brazen woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the memory code from רבי לוי in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children conceived in these flawed situations are the 'rebels' of the פסוק.

steps.title: Challenge: a wife who asks for intimacy produces great children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how 'children of a חצופה' can be a flaw, since רבי יונתן taught that a wife who asks her husband for intimacy will have children greater than those of משה רבינו's generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that true? רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: any man whose wife asks him for intimacy will have children greater than anyone in משה רבינו's generation. משה was told to find 'wise and understanding' men, but in the end only 'wise' men are mentioned, not 'understanding' ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last item on the list, the 'חצופה'. It quotes a teaching that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן praises a wife who asks her husband for intimacy, while the list counts it as a flaw. He begins his proof by showing that even משה could not find 'understanding' men in his generation. That sets up the comparison in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?' A word that opens a challenge.
Understanding people, a level above just wise.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani say
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
Any man whose wife asks him for intimacy
will have children
so great that even in the generation of Moshe our teacher
there were none like them.
As it says: "Get yourselves
wise and understanding men"
and it is written: "So I took the heads of your tribes"
and the word "understanding" is not written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last item on the list, 'children of a חצופה'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a wife's request for intimacy produces flawed children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יונתן teaches that such a request produces outstanding children, the opposite of a flaw.

steps.title: The proof from יששכר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן finishes his proof. יששכר was born after לאה asked יעקב for intimacy, and his descendants had the 'understanding' that משה's generation lacked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'יששכר is a strong-boned donkey.' It is also written: 'From the children of יששכר were men who understood the times.'
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the proof inside the challenge. It shows that children born from a wife's request had the 'understanding' that even משה could not find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The donkey in the פסוק hints at the night לאה went out to יעקב and asked him to come to her, when יששכר was conceived. His descendants are called 'knowers of understanding', the exact trait missing in משה's generation. So a wife's request leads to outstanding children.

phrases.english: And it is written: "Issachar is a strong-boned donkey,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:14. The donkey hints at יעקב riding home when לאה asked him to come to her (בראשית 30:16).

phrases.english: and it is written: "From the children of Issachar,
men who had understanding of the times"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that the challenge of step 13 began.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יונתן's claim that a wife who asks for intimacy has outstanding children.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוקים about יששכר (בראשית 49:14 and דברי הימים א 12:33), set against the missing 'understanding' men in משה's generation.

steps.title: Answer: hinting is praised, openly demanding is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יונתן's praise is for a wife who makes herself pleasing and hints her wish. The 'חצופה' on the list openly demands it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That teaching is about a wife who makes herself pleasing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by showing that the two teachings describe two different kinds of wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both teachings stay true. A wife who shows her desire gently, by making herself pleasing, has excellent children like יששכר. A wife who openly and boldly demands intimacy is the 'חצופה' whose children are on the flawed list.

keyTerms.meaning: She makes herself pleasing and lets him understand her wish without demanding.

steps.whatToRemember: The flawed list describes bad states of mind during intimacy. A wife's wish for intimacy is not a flaw when she hints at it pleasantly. It counts as 'חצופה' only when she openly demands it.

phrases.english: That teaching is about a wife who makes herself pleasing to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 13 and 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two teachings talk about two different kinds of wives.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'חצופה' on the list seemed to include any wife who asks for intimacy, which clashes with רבי יונתן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יונתן praises a wife who hints by making herself pleasing. The 'חצופה' openly demands.

steps.title: הדרן: Closing the פרק of ואלו מותרין
steps.stepSummary: The פרק titled ואלו מותרין ends with the traditional farewell line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק of ואלו מותרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פרק of ואלו מותרין and marks its end with the traditional line, הדרן עלך. Nothing new is argued here. It is a closing marker before a new פרק begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything before this line, including the discussion of the 'rebels' and the חצופה, belonged to the פרק ואלו מותרין. This line closes that unit. The next line is the opening of a brand-new משנה and a new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The traditional words said when finishing a פרק.
'And these are permitted.' This is the name of the פרק being closed, taken from its opening words.

phrases.english: We will return to you, ‘And these are permitted’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק in which the previous steps (the 'rebels' and the חצופה discussion) took place.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק of ואלו מותרין is complete. A new פרק begins next.

steps.title: New פרק: The four kinds of vows that חכמים released
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists four types of נדרים that חכמים treat as not binding: זרוזין, הבאי, שגגות and אונסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים released four kinds of vows: vows meant to push someone, exaggerated vows, mistaken vows, and vows that circumstances beyond one's control prevented.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens the פרק with a list of four kinds of vows that חכמים say are not binding. Each type will be explained one at a time, starting right after this list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four are still spoken in the language of a נדר. The משנה is saying that in these situations the vow does not take hold. The person does not need to go to a חכם to undo it. The list works like a table of contents for the explanations that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים permitted, meaning they treated the vow as not binding.
Vows of urging. A vow used to push or pressure the other person, as in bargaining.
Vows of exaggeration. An obviously overstated vow.
Vows that one was forced out of keeping by circumstances beyond one's control.

steps.confusionAlert: 'הִתִּירוּ' here does not mean that a חכם performed התרת נדרים for a specific person. It means חכמים set a rule that these vows never take hold in the first place.

phrases.english: Four vows the Sages permitted:
Vows of urging, and vows of exaggeration,
and vows of mistakes, and vows of circumstances beyond control.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק right after the הדרן line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four categories of vows (זרוזין, הבאי, שגגות, אונסין) are not binding by rule of חכמים.

steps.title: Example of a vow of urging: haggling over a price
steps.stepSummary: The משנה illustrates נדרי זרוזין with a seller and buyer who each make a קונם vow about the price.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does a vow of urging work? Someone was selling an item and said, 'It should be קונם for me if I lower the price below a סלע.' The buyer answered, 'It should be קונם for me if I pay you more than a שקל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins explaining the first type, נדרי זרוזין, by describing a bargaining scene. This is setup only. The ruling on these two vows comes in the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side uses a קונם vow to show how firm he is, but really he is just pushing the other side in the haggling. The seller wants a full סלע, and the buyer says he won't go past a שקל. The case is built so we can see that neither one truly means his vow.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? The משנה is about to explain with an example.
A word used to make a vow. It makes something forbidden like a קרבן.
A coin. It is worth more than a שקל.
A coin worth half a סלע.
And the other one, meaning the buyer.

phrases.english: Vows of urging, how so?
One was selling an item, and said:
“Konam, that I will not lower for you below the sela,”
phrases.notes: He means: it should be forbidden to me like a קרבן if I take less than a סלע.

phrases.english: and the other one says:
“Konam, that I will not add for you beyond the shekel,”
phrases.notes: A שקל is half a סלע, so the two of them are far apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first item on the list of four.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of נדרי זרוזין: a seller and buyer making opposing קונם vows while bargaining. The ruling follows in the continuation of the משנה.
